name: QUADRILLE
description: Quadrille is a four-player trick-taking game adapted from the Spanish Ombre. The winner of the bidding becomes Hombre, names trump, and may call a King for a partner. The declarer aims to win six of ten tricks using a 40-card pack with inverted red-suit ranking and special matadors (Spadille, Manille, Basta).

content.text: Quadrille is a four-player trick-taking game adapted from the Spanish Ombre. The winner of the bidding becomes Hombre, names trump, and may call a King for a partner. The declarer aims to win six of ten tricks using a 40-card pack with inverted red-suit ranking and special matadors (Spadille, Manille, Basta).

Quadrille was introduced to the southern provinces of France around 1695 and shortly thereafter to Paris. It is an adaptation of the three-player Spanish game Ombre (Hombre) for four players. First English rules appeared in The Game of Quadrille; or Ombre by Four (1720), described as 'the favourite game at the French Court.'
4 players. Each plays for herself; temporary alliances form per deal via the called King.
40 cards: A, K, Q, J, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 in each suit (8s, 9s, 10s removed).
40-card pack, counters or chips for stakes, score sheet.
1. Dealer shuffles; pone cuts. 2. Deal 10 cards each in batches of 4-3-3, 3-4-3, or 3-3-4. 3. Deal and play rotate right (counterclockwise).

items.text: Mediateur: Elaboration of Quadrille with Grandissimo, Nemo, Dimidiator, Casco, and favourite-suit concepts. French rules (1752).
Forced Spadille: When all pass, holder of Spadille (Ace of Spades) becomes Hombre, calls a King for partner. Hombre or partner may name trump. No vole allowed.
Solo / Vole: Solo: Hombre plays alone for six tricks. Vole: bid to take all ten tricks; requires extra stake to a separate pool.
Casco: Bid when holding both Spadille and Basta. Declarer calls a King; the called player names trump. Both play as a team.
